summary:
The starting-pitcher category is the day's biggest red flag across the board. All three ratings are cold on SP — R1 at 43% (81-106, n=187, -6.2pts), R2 identical at 43% (81-106), and R3 at 45% (85-102, -5.8pts) — yet all three carry a 3W streak, which smells like small-sample noise riding on top of a legitimately soft trend. Don't let a short win streak talk you back into SP-driven plays; the 14-day and season gap is too wide to ignore. Meanwhile trends is the anchor category everywhere: 340-290 (54%) season-long on all three ratings, and it pairs best with runs (54.5%, 217-181, n=398) and bullpen (53.5%, 192-167, n=359) for the top combo hit rates today. That said, trends itself is on a 6L streak across all ratings — still profitable long-term, but worth tempering size until it turns.

Strong-play units are bleeding short-term across the board: R1 is -11.0u over 14 days (40-54, 43%) and -7.0u over 30 days, R2 is -9.0u/14d and -8.0u/30d, and R3 is the worst of the three at -13.0u/14d (34-47, 42%) despite still owning the best season number at +26.0u (136-125, 52%). None of the three ratings should be leaned on for strong plays right now — R1's season profit of +18.0u masks a brutal recent slide, and R3's 7-day mark of 13-23 (36%) is the coldest window in the entire sheet. If you're overriding model caution today, do it through team trust: TBR strong plays are elite at 18-5 (78%, +22.0u), LAD strong plays are hitting 11-2 (85%, +14.0u), and BOS remains rock-solid at 72% overall (26-10) with +7.0u on strong plays. Fade HOU strong plays outright — 3-8 (27%, -8.0u) is the one team leaderboard number working against the model, not for it.
